spot: Rocky Face summit (granitic dome high point)

detail.reason: Summit ~1795-1818 ft, ~600 ft above the Piedmont, prominence 607 ft; literally the high point with views down onto lower ground. Directly matches the single dominant signature.
Large bare dome with views in ALL directions over valleys; on clear days Grandfather, Table Rock, Hawksbill, Black Mtns. A true wide open panorama, not enclosed.

Dome has exfoliation sheet-joints and shallow cracks, but a broad bare rounded dome offers few deep undercut/overhang recesses; niche caching is plausible but not its strong feature (quarry-cliff base fits this better).
Shallow-soil bald over bare granite; a box can rest on/against the rock at surface level, no digging possible on the dome anyway.
Entire spot IS stone - broad bare granite dome, flat standable rock platforms, picnic tables on the granite; stone is unambiguously the host feature.
Dry exfoliating dome bald; only vernal pools after rain. No creek/river/pond/spring adjacent or below at the summit; the streams are downslope. Highest-support constraint, and it does not match here.
The dome is an open rock bald (clearing) ringed by Piedmont monadnock forest, so forest-meets-open is present, but the spot itself is the open rock, not a forest edge just past a tree line.
Reached on the established Hollow Rock Trail / Vertical Mile route, ~1-2.5 mi on foot, non-dangerous footing. Clean match.
Well under 3 mi from Rocky Face Church Rd, reachable on foot in well under 2 hrs, no water crossing or cliff scaling to stand on the dome.
Summit dome is the most visited, most obvious destination with picnic tables and 360 views - the opposite of secluded/off the obvious line of sight.
A rounded dome high point, not a gap/saddle/notch between paired crags. No cinched landform framing the spot.
Red cedar grows on the dome margins, but the summit is bare rock; no single prominent oak/pine as the operative marker at the spot.
Dome has views in all directions including east, but it is not specifically east-oriented; named long views are to the N and W (Pores Knob N, Black Mtns W).
The defining form is a rounded/domed bornhardt - 'a rounded dome not a peaked summit.' Strong literal echo of the rounded-stone shape cue.
Lichens and dry rock moss against light-grey/darker exposed granite; classic moss-on-stone color contrast across the bald.
Granitic gneiss is hard, durable, quartz-bearing with mica glint, so the host material qualifies, but it is not notably sparkling/crystal-display rock.
The dome is characteristically SMOOTH and rounded with sheet-joints - the opposite of sharp angular/faceted/columnar rock.
Rock is light-grey, not reddish; however spring reddish mats of elf orpine provide a warm-toned color cue on the dome surface.
'Broad bare light-grey rock' - pale light stone standing against darker forest/soil surroundings. Direct match.
Vernal pools are small basin/cup depressions in the rock, a weak match to the bowl/hollow cue; no large amphitheater cove.
No confluence or watercourse bend at or below the summit; drainage divides flow off the dome, no two waters meeting here.
Approach to the summit is a sustained ascent, not a 'go down then up' pattern; no final descent into a draw before the high spot.
Exfoliation seams/cracks could serve as fine confirming marks, but no known inscription; speculative for the bare dome.
No specific left-turn decision nudge tied to the summit approach in the spot data.
An exposed breezy granite dome bald, fully open to wind/rain rather than a sealed cave - exactly the open-to-elements profile.
No fixed marker-to-spot pace count applies to an open featureless dome top; nothing concrete to count from.
